title: onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent
why_read: A clever, cheap hardware hack that lets a vision-capable AI model control a real iPhone's screen and inputs using a $7 microcontroller, with no jailbreak or developer account needed.
analysis: The project uses AirPlay to mirror the iPhone's screen to an ESP32 board which feeds frames to any OpenAI-compatible vision model, and uses USB HID emulation to send touch and button inputs back to the phone. This is a neat demonstration of treating a phone purely as a black box of screen output and input events, sidestepping Apple's usual restrictions on automation and accessibility APIs. It's a good example of low-cost hardware bridging being used for AI agent automation, relevant to people interested in physical automation, agentic AI, or hardware hacking. The $7 price point and lack of jailbreak requirement make it unusually accessible for hobbyists to replicate.
